provenance: Assignment author review: examined complete new rules and concrete example propositions together with their setup definitions. Reviewed fixed binding metadata, partial-view store updates, RHS-first ordering, runtime writable/replaceable guards, frame GC and forward Destructor embedding. Explicitly retained the demonstrated older-ID invariant failure and missing Assignment soundness/reflection as future proof obligations. Existing claims and selected sources were compared byte-for-byte with prior reviewed packets; new AGENTS scope and SUMMARY insertion were inspected. This is differential author review for unchanged units, not an independent review. CLI workers only partition immutable evidence preparation/recording; no subagents were used.
rationale: The landing md/shared.md#claim-shared.references directly introduces Shared reference modes and reference/slot representation. Introduces reference mode and pair representation before give uses them. Tagged object identities link back to their standalone Given definition; no object-level ownership flag is implied. κ/r/s are defined by their local grammar. ObjectId and obj(n) use the tagged-number convention linked to Given, not a mode attached to the object record. Prerequisites are linked in the retained chapter; the selected body states this subject rather than asking the reader to find a definition elsewhere in a multipurpose chapter. Assignment insertion shifts subsequent chapter positions but leaves existing authored passages, targets, relative concept order and prior classifications unchanged. Required non-audit inputs were compared exactly, except the reviewed SUMMARY and AGENTS updates.
limitations: Author editorial self-review. Extraction and byte ranges do not establish clarity by themselves. Earlier unchanged passages retain the prior review after exact-input comparison. Future notes remain nonnormative.
